Title: Modjeska Simkins Papers, General Papers, 1940-1949
Creator: Simkins, Modjeska Monteith, 1899-1992
Source: Modjeska Simkins Papers. Series: General Papers. South Carolina Political Collections.
Keywords: Olin D. (Olin Dewitt), 1896-1965; Graham, Frank Porter, 1886-1972; Taft, Robert A. (Robert Alphonso), 1889-1953; Lindeman, Eduard; Southern Negro Youth; sharecroppers; Congress; Southern Congress on Human Welfare; National Association for the Advancement of Colored People;
Description: In addition to several personal letters from Simkins to her step-children and in-laws, this folder contains materials related to her care for, and death of, an elderly friend named Earnest Garnes. Of special interest are an open letter in which she challenges Governor Olin Johnston to debate his racist views, letters from North Carolina Senator Frank Graham and educational pioneer Eduard Lindeman asking her to contribute to the Natoinal Sharecroppers Fund, and a letter from Ohio Senator Robert Taft thanking her voting for him at the 1948 Republican National Convention. During the 1940s, Simkins became State Secretary for the NAACP and became more active in voter registration drives and regional politics. Letters related to her involvement with the Southern Conference on Human Welfare and the Southern Negro Youth Congress also appear in this folder. There is also a letter from a committe that included Paul Robeson, Benjamin Mays, and W.E.B. DuBois inviting her to a meeting of black leaders in New York on November 8, 1947.

Description: This folder contains several personal letters to and from Modjeska Simkins. Some of these letters deal with her husband Andrew's family affairs. Items of interest include a letter to Eleanor Roosevelt asking her for an audience during her visit to Columbia. There are also two letters to Franklin Roosevelt asking him to remember Gov. Olin Johnston's racism when consulting him on federal appointments. Finally, there are several letters related Simkins's job with the Negro Program for the South Carolina Tubercolisis Association. in addition to the letters, the folder contains a few postcards, including one showing the Benedict College campus during hte 1910s.

Title: Modjeska Simkins Papers, General Papers, 1964-1966
Creator: Simkins, Modjeska Monteith, 1899-1992
Source: Modjeska Simkins Papers. Series: General Papers. South Carolina Political Collections.
Keywords: Russell, Donald; Bates, Lester; Aptheker, Herbert; Watson, Albert; employmnet discrimination; Democratic Party
Description: This folder features many items pertaining to Simkins's political activity. She frequently helped those who felt their civil rights had been violated. For example, she wrote letters to the U.S. Department of Justice regarding unfair employment practices at both Ft. Jackson and the State Mental Hospital. Simkins herself ran for the city council and for the South Caraolina House of Representatives 1966. This folder also features letters pertaining to the controversy over her support of Herbert Aptheker, a Marxist historian. She befriended Aptheker while he was stationed at Ft. Jackson during World War II. Finally, the folder contains some letters to and from such well-known South Carolina political figures as Governor Donald Russell and Columbia Mayor Lester Bates. Although neither man was a staunch supporter of African American rights, both men counted on African American votes to win election.

Title: Modjeska Simkins Papers, General Papers, 1957-1963
Creator: Simkins, Modjeska Monteith, 1899-1992
Source: Modjeska Simkins Papers. Series: General Papers. South Carolina Political Collections.
Keywords: civil rights; Elloree, SC; Henri Monteith; Henry Monteith; voter education; Hollings, Ernest F.; Russell, Donald; Small Business Administration
Description: This folder contains a number of letters regarding Modjeska Simkins's business dealings. For example, she loaned money to several people facing hardship. This hardship at least in some cases appears to be the result of reprisals for civil rights activity in Elloree, South Carolina. There are also letters pertaining to voter registration and education initiatives. African American votes were becoming more important to South Carolina politicians, and the folder includes a letter from Donald Russell asking for support against Fritz Hollings in the 1958 gubernatorial election. There are a couple of letters from white supremacist groups, including one sent to Dr. Henry Monteith, Simkins's brother, asking for donations to the White Citizens' Council. Monteith's daughter, Henri, would integrate the University of South Carolina in the Fall of 1963. There are some letters pertaining to violations of civil rights in South Carolina, including the electrocution of Walter James Outen for allegedly raping a white woman. The Teachers Union of New York City always invited Simkins to its annual meeting, and letters pertaining to that topic also appear in the folder. On a more personal note, the folder contains several letters expressing condolences over the death of Monteith's mother.

Description: Most of the items in this folder relate biogrpahical information on Modjeska Simkins, including several newspaper or magazine articles. There are a few items related to her funeral, including an article in The State  from April 10, 1992. The folder also incldues an encyclopedia entry from historian and Clemson University professor Orville Vernon Burton. It also contains a certificate from Columbia mayor Bob Coble, declaring December 5, 1991 Modjeska Simkins Day. There is also an interview about Ms. Simkins with George B. Murphy, Jr., editor of the Washington Afro-American. Finally, the folder includes two of Simkins's passports.
